title: apideck.com/blog/quickbooks-api-pricing-and-the-intuit-app-partner-program
snippet:
Intuit introduced a significant change in 2025 with the launch of the [Intuit App Partner Program](https://blogs.intuit.com/2025/05/15/introducing-the-intuit-app-partner-program/). This new program introduces a tiered pricing model that distinguishes between different types of API operations, offering free unlimited access for data creation and updates while implementing usage-based pricing for data retrieval operations.

### Core API Calls (Free & Unlimited)
- **What they include**: Most data-in operations such as creating or updating records
- **Examples**: POST requests to create/update invoices, bills, customers, vendors, accounts, payments, etc.
- **Pricing**: Completely free and unlimited across all partner tiers
- **HTTP Methods**: Primarily POST operations for pushing data into QuickBooks
### CorePlus API Calls (Metered & Charged)
- **What they include**: Most data-out operations such as reading and querying data
- **Examples**: GET requests to retrieve accounts, query company information, fetch reports, read invoices, etc.
- **Pricing**: Free up to certain monthly limits, then charged based on usage
- **HTTP Methods**: Primarily GET operations for downloading data from QuickBooks
## Partner Tiers and Pricing Structure
The new program includes four partner tiers with different pricing models:
![QuickBooks API pricing](//images.ctfassets.net/d6o5ai4eeewt/5eevWdLgBlQSRMYEYg9SeM/2a81456f9f006dbab42dec1b199f66b2/Screenshot_2025-09-20_at_14.16.11.png)
### Builder Tier (Free)
- **Monthly Fee**: $0
- **Core API Calls**: Unlimited (free)
- **CorePlus API Credits**: 500,000 per month
- **Overage**: API calls are **blocked** after exceeding the 500,000 limit
- **Premium API Access**: Not included
- **Best For**: Small developers and those just getting started
### Silver Tier
- **Monthly Fee**: $300
- **Core API Calls**: Unlimited (free)
- **CorePlus API Credits**: 1 million per month (~$3,500 worth)
- **Overage Rate**: $3.50 per 1,000 API calls
- **Premium API Access**: Yes - Projects, Custom Fields, Sales Tax, Time with Payroll
- **Best For**: Growing applications with moderate data retrieval needs
### Gold Tier
- **Monthly Fee**: $1,700
- **Core API Calls**: Unlimited (free)
- **CorePlus API Credits**: Higher allocation than Silver
- **Overage Rate**: Better rates than Silver tier
- **Premium API Access**: Yes - Projects, Custom Fields, Sales Tax, Time with Payroll
- **Additional Benefits**: Allocated partner team, improved support

title: Can you provide QuickBooks API access for historical client data to build our internal dashboard, including any API limits, restrictions, and charges? | QuickBooks Community
snippet:
Yes, you can pull historical accounting and transaction data into your dashboard through the QuickBooks Online Accounting API, and setting up developer access itself is free. Here's how each piece works.
### Getting API access
1. Create a free account at the [Intuit Developer Portal](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbo/docs/get-started/start-developing-your-app), separate from your regular QuickBooks Online login.
2. From your developer dashboard, create an app and select QuickBooks Online. This generates your client ID and client secret, plus a free sandbox company for testing.
3. Each of your clients' QuickBooks Online companies will need to individually connect and authorize your app through OAuth 2.0, since access is scoped per company (per "realm ID"). There's no single connection that pulls data across all your managed clients at once, so each client authorizes the connection to their own books.

API access itself runs on a separate track from your QuickBooks Online subscription, through Intuit's App Partner Program. As of this program's rollout, API calls are split into two types:
- **Core calls** (mostly creating or updating records) are free and unmetered on every tier.
- **CorePlus calls** (mostly reading data and pulling reports, which is what your dashboard would rely on) are metered. The free Builder tier includes 500,000 CorePlus calls per month at no cost. Beyond that, paid tiers (Silver, Gold, Platinum) add higher monthly credit allotments with per-call overage pricing.
For a reporting dashboard like yours, you'd likely start on the free Builder tier and only need to consider a paid tier if your combined client data volume pushes past that monthly CorePlus allowance.

title: QuickBooks API: Setup, Pricing and Errors (2026 Guide)
snippet:
The QuickBooks API is [Intuit](https://www.intuit.com/oidam/intuit/ic/en_us/content/intuit-fact-sheet-document-icom-20240401.pdf)'s REST interface for reading and writing a QuickBooks Online company's accounting data, and it is the same interface that no-code tools such as [Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com) call behind the scenes.
Access needs a free Intuit developer account and an app, and each customer's company authorizes that app. Checked 19 Nov 2026 against [Intuit's developer docs](https://developer.intuit.com).

| Plan | Price per month | Users included | API access (checked 19 Nov 2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Simple Start | $38 | 1 | App can connect |
| Essentials | $85 | 3 | App can connect |
| Plus | $140 | 5 | App can connect |

Intuit meters API calls by tier, and the cost doesn't scale in a straight line. [Tierguard](https://tierguard.dev/guides/quickbooks-api-cost) puts the Silver-tier bill at $300 a month for 1M calls, which is a modest line item.

The free plan includes unlimited flows and 1,000 credits a month, so you can set the connection up and try it without paying anything.

**Is the QuickBooks API free to use?**
Creating an Intuit developer account and a sandbox company hasn't required payment. Intuit has changed how it prices API access, so confirm the current terms on Intuit's developer pricing page before you build.
Then ask who pays: the connection belongs to a specific QuickBooks company, and the cost should sit with whoever owns it.

title: apideck.com/blog/exploring-the-quickbooks-online-accounting-api.md
snippet:
Writes are free, but since July 2025 reads (CorePlus calls) are metered under Intuit's App Partner Program, with 500,000 free per month on the Builder tier (see the pricing section below). Requests are throttled at 500 per minute and 10 per second per company. Intuit also provides free sandbox companies, up to 10 per developer account. If you want to use it with your own real QuickBooks account, you have to purchase a paid QuickBooks plan to create an account. Pricing for QuickBooks Online [varies depending on the plan](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/pricing/?cid=cdist_wblog_id).

Intuit fundamentally transformed the QuickBooks Online API landscape in 2025 with the introduction of the Intuit App Partner Program, marking the end of free unlimited API access that developers had previously enjoyed. The new tiered pricing model creates a clear distinction between Core API calls (data creation and updates like creating invoices or customers) which remain completely free and unlimited, and CorePlus API calls (data retrieval operations like querying accounts or fetching reports) which are now metered and charged based on usage. The program offers four partner tiers ranging from the free Builder tier with 500,000 monthly CorePlus API credits to the Platinum tier with up to 75 million credits and enhanced support. While this represents a significant shift for QuickBooks Online integrations, developers can optimize costs by focusing on efficient querying practices, and carefully analyzing their GET versus POST request ratios to select the most appropriate tier for their needs. For a comprehensive breakdown of the pricing structure, API classifications, and migration strategies, developers should consult our detailed analysis of [QuickBooks API pricing and the Intuit App Partner Program](https://www.apideck.com/blog/quickbooks-api-pricing-and-the-intuit-app-partner-program).

title: QuickBooks API Integration (2026): Options, Pricing, Walkthrough
snippet:
### Online Accounting API
A hosted REST API. You register an app on Intuit's developer portal, the user approves access once on Intuit's consent page, and your software calls `https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/{realmId}/...` with a bearer token. It has a SQL-like query language, full create, read, update and delete on customers, items, invoices, bills, payments and the rest, and reports. This is the one to build on if you run QuickBooks Online.

Since Intuit's App Partner Program started charging on 1 November 2025, API calls come in two kinds. **Core** calls put data in (creating or updating records) and are free and unlimited on every tier. **CorePlus** calls take data out (queries, reads, reports) and are metered.
| Tier | Monthly fee | CorePlus reads included | Above that |
|---|---|---|---|
| Builder | $0 | 500,000 a month | Blocked until next month |
| Silver | $300 | 1 million | $3.50 per 1,000 up to 10 million |
| Gold | $1,700 | 10 million | $1.40 per 1,000 up to 75 million |
| Platinum | $4,500 | 75 million | $0.25 per 1,000 |

The API calls are the small part: free on Intuit's Builder tier for most single-business integrations. The work is in matching your data to QuickBooks', handling what can't be matched, and deciding who approves what. Our published prices:
| | Price | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed-price starter | **$1,900** | One QuickBooks workflow on your own company file, about two weeks, credited against a production build |
| Scoping | $2,300 to $4,700 | The workflow mapped, matching and approval rules defined, a fixed quote |
| First workflow in production | From $17,500 | Live and monitored, then from about $470 a month to run |
| Migration or simpler sync | From $5,000 | Quoted as a [first slice of custom software](https://reflektlab.ai/solutions/custom-erp-development/) |
